merger_description:
Vital Bidco AB and/or Vital Holdco AB (together, **Vital**) propose to acquire 100% of the issued share capital of EMPWR Nutrition Group NV (**EMPWR**) (the **Acquisition**).

Vital HoldCo AB and its subsidiaries (which includes the acquirer, Vital Bidco AB) (**Vitamin Well Group**) are indirectly solely controlled by Cinven Limited via the Eighth Cinven Fund (**Cinven**). Cinven is a private equity firm engaged in the provision of investment management and investment advisory services to several investment funds. The controlled companies in the Cinven funds’ portfolio of investments are active in a wide range of sectors including business services, consumer, financial services, healthcare, industrials and technology, media and telecommunications.

The Cinven funds’ portfolio of investments includes Vitamin Well Group and Barentz. Vitamin Well Group is a Swedish functional food and beverage company that develops and sells functional food and beverages, primarily through its three core brands: Vitamin Well (vitamin and mineral-enriched drinks), NOCCO (functional drinks) and Barebells (protein bars and protein drinks).

Barentz is a Netherlands headquartered company that is a global specialty ingredients solution provider specialising in human nutrition, pharmaceuticals, personal care, performance materials and animal nutrition. Barentz is a supplier and distributor of raw materials and specialty ingredients.

EMPWR is a Belgium headquartered company who is globally active as a developer and contract manufacturer of functional snack bars, including protein bars, uncoated dough bars, granola bars, crisp bars, nut bars, and fruit bars at the business-to-business level for brand-owners and retailers mainly across Europe and North America. EMPWR co-designs, develops, and manufactures bars on a private-label basis at its production sites in Croatia, the Netherlands, Canada and the United States.

EMPWR is currently majority owned by WPEF VI Holdco I BE B.V. and is indirectly held by funds managed by Waterland Private Equity Investments B.V. (**Waterland**). Waterland is a Dutch private equity investment company.

determination_table_content.details:
Vital Bidco AB and Vital Holdco AB (together, Vital) applied for a
notification waiver in respect of Vital Bidco AB and/or Vital Holdco
AB’s proposed acquisition of 100% of the issued share capital of
EMPWR Nutrition Group NV (EMPWR), as described in the
transaction documents provided as part of the application (the
Acquisition).

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABV(1)(a) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.

Vital Holdco AB and its subsidiaries (which includes the acquirer
Vital Bidco AB) (Vitamin Well Group) are indirectly solely controlled
by Cinven Limited via the Eighth Cinven Fund.
Cinven is a private equity firm engaged in the provision of investment
management and investment advisory services to several
investment funds. The controlled companies in the Cinven funds’
portfolio of investments are active in a wide range of sectors
including business services, consumer, financial services, healthcare,
industrials and technology, media and telecommunications.
The Cinven funds’ portfolio of investments includes Vitamin Well
Group and Barentz. Vitamin Well Group is a Swedish functional food
and beverage company that develops and sells functional food and
beverages, primarily through its three core brands: Vitamin Well
(vitamin and mineral-enriched drinks), NOCCO (functional drinks)
and Barebells (protein bars and protein drinks). Vitamin Well Group
is not active in the contract manufacturing of functional snack bars
for third-party brands.
Barentz is a Netherlands headquartered company that is a global
specialty ingredients solution provider specialising in human
nutrition, pharmaceuticals, personal care, performance materials and
animal nutrition. Barentz is a supplier and distributor of raw
materials and specialty ingredients.
The target, EMPWR, is a Belgium headquartered company who is
globally active as a developer and contract manufacturer of
functional snack bars, including protein bars, uncoated dough bars,
granola bars, crisp bars, nut bars, and fruit bars at the business-to-
business level for brand-owners and retailers mainly across Europe
and North America. EMPWR co-designs, develops, and manufactures
bars on a private-label basis at its production sites in Croatia, the
Netherlands, Canada and the United States.

In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
certain publicly available information, and had regard to the factors
in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition and Consumer Act 2010
(Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information currently before it, the ACCC considers that
the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material lessening of
competition. In particular:
a. there is no horizontal overlap between Vitamin Well Group
(including its connected entities) and EMPWR in the supply
of functional snack bar manufacturing or broader food
manufacturing in Australia
b. there are alternative manufacturers of functional snack bars,
and suppliers of functional snack bars, in Australia
c. there is a low risk of foreclosure or other concerning vertical
effects resulting from exclusionary conduct in Australia
post-acquisition.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
